'''''Barbula convoluta''''', also called '''''Streblotrichum convolutum,''''' less commonly known as '''lesser bird's-claw beard-moss''' and '''Convoluted Beard Moss''' is a species of [[moss]] belonging the family [[Pottiaceae]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Qian |first=Hong |url=https://www.google.co.kr/books/edition/Plants_of_British_Columbia/cBciWJHM5GkC?hl=ko&gbpv=1&dq=Barbula+unguiculata&pg=PA207&printsec=frontcover |title=Plants of British Columbia: Scientific and Common Names of Vascular Plants, Bryophytes, and Lichens |last2=Klinka |first2=K. |date=1998 |publisher=UBC Press |isbn=978-0-7748-0652-7 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Barbula convoluta / Species Page / Plant Atlas |url=https://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/plant/species/4611 |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=florida.plantatlas.usf.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Segal |first=S. |url=https://www.google.co.kr/books/edition/Ecological_Notes_on_Wall_Vegetation/EQ79CAAAQBAJ?hl=ko&gbpv=1&dq=Streblotrichum+convolutum&pg=PA252&printsec=frontcover |title=Ecological Notes on Wall Vegetation |date=2013-11-11 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-94-017-6232-8 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Webmaster |first=David Ratz |title=Convoluted Beard Moss - Montana Field Guide |url=https://fieldguide.mt.gov/speciesDetail.aspx?elcode=NBMUS0Q070 |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=fieldguide.mt.gov |language=en}}</ref> The [[leaves]] are between {{Convert|0.5|mm|in}} and {{Convert|1.5|mm|in}} in length and are broadly lanceolate or more parallel-sided. The leaves become firm when wet. The stems are {{Convert|1 to 1.5|cm|in}}. The [[seta]] is slender and yellow, and measured about {{Convert|1 to 1.8|cm|in}}, the [[theca]] is {{Convert|0.8 to 1.2|mm|in}}, and the [[spore]]s are smooth and measured about 10 to 12 micrometers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barbula convoluta - FNA |url=https://floranorthamerica.org/Barbula_convoluta |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=Flora Borth America }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Flora of New Zealand {{!}} Taxon Profile {{!}} Streblotrichum convolutum |url=https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/Taxon/Streblotrichum-convolutum.html |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=www.nzflora.info}}</ref> Capsules are not common, but it can fruit abundantly with yellow [[seta]]e and sheathing.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Streblotrichum convolutum - British Bryological Society |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/streblotrichum-convolutum/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427231518/https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/streblotrichum-convolutum/ |archive-date=2025-04-27 |access-date=2025-11-07 |work=British Bryological Society |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Barbula convoluta'' is very common and sometimes grows in great abundance. It is found in exposed sites, mainly in urban settings, on [[soil]], [[Sand dunes|sand]], [[gravel]], granite, [[brick]]s, walls, [[sandstone]], [[limestone]], dunes, paths and [[boulder]]s.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Associated mosses include ''[[Barbula unguiculata]]'', ''[[Bryum argenteum]]'', ''[[Ceratodon purpureus]]'', and ''[[Tortula muralis]]''.<ref name=":1" />
